name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,330

clue.text: Oily excretion around sore toe, possibly

indicators.note: 'possibly' says the letters might be arranged some other way than as written

blocks.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A greasy discharge has appeared round someone's painful toe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a container signal, but here it simply gives C, for circa.
explanation.definitionFit: Creosote is the oily liquid distilled from tar, the kind of substance wood and coal give off.

clue.text: Look after Snitch caught by Potter?

indicators.note: something caught by another is held inside it

blocks.note: a potter in snooker sinks balls, using a cue
a rat is an informer, someone who snitches

explanation.surface: Harry Potter must mind the Golden Snitch he has caught in Quidditch.
explanation.walkthrough: The Harry Potter picture is misdirection: the potter is a snooker cue.
explanation.definitionFit: To curate is to look after a collection or exhibition, selecting and caring for it.

clue.text: Use them over carry on bags

indicators.note: to bag something is to put it in a bag, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: 'em is informal for them
to ply a trade is to carry it on
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Use those spare bags for your hand luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carry on bags' looks like airline luggage; the phrase splits into a verb and a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To employ something is to make use of it, as in employing a tool.

clue.text: A run down car, perhaps, abandoned here?

definitions.text: A run down car, perhaps, abandoned here?

indicators.note: run down here means with the run taken away, run being the cricket abbreviation removed from the word
abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so these letters are let loose into a new order

blocks.note: the word with R, short for run, taken out
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old banger might well be dumped somewhere like this.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a run-down car is just what gets abandoned at this place. R is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a run.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrapheap is a pile of discarded metal and junk, where worn-out cars end their days.

clue.text: New TV show let me broadcast for a year

indicators.note: to broadcast is to scatter widely, as seed is sown, so these letters land in a new order

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
letters to be rearranged
letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A presenter asks to air a new television programme for a whole year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' fits the TV picture perfectly, which hides its role as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve months make up one calendar year, so the phrase is a straight equivalent.

clue.text: Plunder silver during house party

indicators.note: something happening during an event sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a rave is a big dance party, often to house music
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Burglars make off with the silverware while a party is going on.
explanation.definitionFit: To ravage a place is to lay it waste and plunder it, as raiders do.

clue.text: Adding beans analogue calculators improved initially

definitions.text: Adding beans analogue calculators improved initially

indicators.note: initially points to the start of each word, so only their opening letters are kept

blocks.note: the first letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: Counting with beans got better once mechanical calculators arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: abaci are analogue calculators that improved on counting with beans.
explanation.definitionFit: Abaci are counting frames with beads on rods, early hand-worked calculating devices.

clue.text: Appetiser raising passion in attractive assistant

indicators.note: in places the passion between the two words of the phrase that follows
in a down clue raising lifts the letters upward, so they read from bottom to top

blocks.note: fit is British slang for attractive
ire is anger, a fierce passion
a PA is a personal assistant

explanation.surface: Someone arousing desire in a good-looking assistant.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is a drink taken before a meal to sharpen the appetite.

clue.text: Mobile network features really relating to the masses

indicators.note: something that features another includes it, so that piece sits inside

blocks.note: EE is a British mobile phone network
really and very both intensify
on means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A phone network's ads are genuinely aimed at ordinary people.
explanation.definitionFit: Everyone means all people, the whole populace or the masses taken together.

clue.text: Banter concerning involvement with drugs

blocks.note: re means regarding or about
to have a part in something is to be involved
E is slang for a tablet of ecstasy, and drugs plural makes two of them

explanation.surface: Someone is talking about their role in a drugs case.
explanation.definitionFit: Repartee is quick witty conversation, the same playful exchange as banter.

clue.text: Cell willing to exterminate leaders

indicators.note: the leaders of words are the letters at their heads, so only first letters count

blocks.note: to be game is to be willing to have a go
the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A cell ready to wipe out its bosses sounds like a terrorist plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cell' suggests a terrorist group; it is the biological kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamete is a reproductive cell, such as a sperm or egg.

clue.text: Boastful in log about many embraces

indicators.note: letters turned about are moved around into a new order
something that embraces another holds it inside

blocks.note: various means many and different
letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A ship's log brags about all the hugs given on board.
explanation.definitionFit: Vainglorious means excessively proud of oneself, given to boasting and showing off.

clue.text: Best clothing from limited company

indicators.note: a limited word is kept within bounds, so its outer letters are cut away
a thing clothing another wraps around it, so one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: top means the best
the word with its first and last letters removed

explanation.surface: Fine garments sold by a limited company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited company' reads as a firm, but 'limited' works on 'from' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A troop is a company of soldiers or a group of people, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Against talent concealing one's likelihood of success

indicators.note: something concealing another hides it inside itself, so one piece goes in

blocks.note: v is short for versus, against
a talent is an ability
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone resistant to talent is hiding their own chances of getting on.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Viability is the capacity of a plan or business to work out and survive.

clue.text: Terminate construction breaks following working unrest

indicators.note: a construction is something built up from parts, so these letters are reassembled
one thing breaking another splits it open and sits in the gap

blocks.note: f is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
letters to be rearranged
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Building work is halted after trouble among the workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terminate construction' reads as halting a building project; the first word is the fodder and the second its signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Fermentation figuratively means agitation or turmoil, a state of social unrest.

clue.text: Radio station employee can run one off

indicators.note: something off is out of order or wrong, so these letters need reordering

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A radio worker is able to run a programme off on their own.
explanation.definitionFit: An announcer introduces programmes and reads news on air, a job at a broadcaster.

clue.text: Kind of shot English Sunday papers love

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
S is the abbreviation for Sunday
the press is the newspapers
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: The English Sunday newspapers adore a particular kind of photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' suggests a photo in the papers; it is a shot of coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: An espresso is strong coffee served in a small single measure called a shot.

clue.text: Where to take off apron and strip?

definitions.text: Where to take off apron and strip?

blocks.note: surface reading: removing an apron and undressing
setter's reading: a place where planes leave the ground, with an apron for parking and a strip for runways

explanation.walkthrough: An apron is the paved area where aircraft park and a strip is a runway, so the undressing picture is all aviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An airfield is an area of land where aircraft take off and land, with runways and parking.

clue.text: Water's way of helping in spa treatment?

indicators.note: giving something a treatment works it over, so these letters get reworked

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Is a dip in the water part of the help on offer at a health spa?
explanation.walkthrough: The spa and water point to bathing; the water is the sea and its way is a route for ships.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipping lane is a regular route at sea used by vessels, a path through the water.

clue.text: Bullets hidden in case of German meat

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, so only the outer letters are kept
something hidden in another is tucked inside it

blocks.note: the first and last letters
ammo is short for ammunition

explanation.surface: Ammunition has been smuggled inside a German's luggage of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Gammon is cured or smoked ham, cut from the hind leg of a pig.

clue.text: Session with medium amount of drink after skipping round?

indicators.note: skipping something passes over it, and a round letter is the ring-shaped one, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: the drink is crossword slang for the sea, and a sea of something is a vast amount
once can mean as soon as, or after, as in 'once you've eaten'

explanation.surface: A meeting where someone drinks a middling measure after missing a round at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: The round is the letter O, not a round of drinks; and the definition borrows 'medium' from the drinking picture to mean a spiritualist.
explanation.definitionFit: A seance is a meeting at which a medium tries to contact the dead.

clue.text: Student chasing alternatives to free drink

indicators.note: alternatives here means alternate letters, taking every second one
one thing chasing another comes behind it, so that piece goes second

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters
a fresher is a first-year university student

explanation.surface: A student goes after other options than a free drink.
explanation.walkthrough: FRESHER is British for a first-year student, a freshman.
explanation.definitionFit: A refresher is a drink taken to revive oneself, as in a quick refreshment.

clue.text: Weariness seen in pupil now and again

indicators.note: now and again means at intervals, so only every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the even-placed letters, starting from the second

explanation.surface: Tiredness is noticed in a schoolchild from time to time.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless boredom and dissatisfaction, a world-weary feeling.

clue.text: Interest of old uranium plant

blocks.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium
sage is a herb

explanation.surface: Curiosity about a former uranium processing plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests a nuclear works; it is the herb.
explanation.definitionFit: In archaic English usage meant the charging of interest on money lent, what is now usury.

clue.text: Sets out to collect fashionable mugs

indicators.note: letters set out are laid out afresh, in a different order
to collect something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged
in means in fashion

explanation.surface: Someone goes off to gather some trendy coffee cups.
explanation.definitionFit: Steins are large earthenware beer mugs of German origin.

clue.text: Staff positioned behind train driver

indicators.note: a piece positioned behind another comes after it in the answer

blocks.note: to coach is to train
to man a post is to staff it

explanation.surface: Workers sit at the back of a train, behind the driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train driver' reads as one phrase; the train is the verb and the driver stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A coachman drives a horse-drawn carriage.

clue.text: Establish insomnia (drowsiness has returned)

indicators.note: these words have the letters within them, running across the word break
something returned goes back the way it came, so read right to left

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A sleepless spell is confirmed when sleepiness comes back.
explanation.definitionFit: To ordain is to decree or lay down, establishing something by authority.

clue.text: Cut off sergeant manoeuvres

indicators.note: troops in manoeuvres move around, so these letters are moved into a new order

blocks.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An army NCO on exercises is isolated from the unit.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange someone is to alienate them, cutting them off from family or friends.
